get.description:
Process is up and serving requests. Does not probe external dependencies; with Entra
ID SSO enabled it reads one marker from the auth store (``warnings``).
Public keys that verify KERP tokens (RFC 7517). Contains no private material.

post.description: Exchange email + password for an access token (15 min) and a refresh token.

429.description: Locked after repeated failures; retry after `Retry-After` seconds

401.description: Not authenticated; with `code: DEVICE_REVOKED` when `X-KERP-Device-Id` (or the session's device) is revoked: wipe the device's local data. Sign-in answers `DEVICE_REVOKED` only after the credentials are right

post.description:
Send a one-time sign-in link (15 min) to a field worker's e-mail.

Always ``202`` (unknown, inactive and other-tenant addresses included), so the answer
reveals no accounts.

429.description: Locked after repeated failures; retry after `Retry-After` seconds

post.description:
Spend a magic link: start a session. On an enrolled device (`X-KERP-Device-Id`) it is
bound to that device at once; the device's PIN stays as it is.

401.description: Not authenticated; with `code: DEVICE_REVOKED` when `X-KERP-Device-Id` (or the session's device) is revoked: wipe the device's local data. Sign-in answers `DEVICE_REVOKED` only after the credentials are right

post.description:
Renew a session of a device with a PIN: the device's refresh token + the PIN.

Wrong PINs lock the device's PIN unlock progressively (offline failures reported in
`failed_offline` count too); the 10th wrong PIN ends PIN unlock on the device until the
next sign-in there. Nothing is revoked and nothing is wiped.

429.description: Locked after repeated failures; retry after `Retry-After` seconds

401.description: Not authenticated. With `code`: `PIN_REQUIRED` (refresh: idle too long, unlock with the PIN), `PIN_INVALID` (unlock: wrong PIN), `PIN_EXHAUSTED` (unlock: the 10th wrong PIN, sign in again on this device), `DEVICE_REVOKED` (wipe the device)

post.description:
Rotate: the refresh token is spent and a new pair is issued. Reuse revokes the session.

The new refresh token keeps the session's end (sign-in + 12 h); after it, sign in again.
The web SPA sends the cookie; an allow-listed native app sends ``refresh_token``. A
session of a device with a PIN that was idle too long gets `401 {code: PIN_REQUIRED}`
(the token is not spent: unlock with it and the PIN).

The sign-in methods: Entra ID SSO as the preferred one when the deployment offers it,

Start an Entra ID sign-in: a redirect to the company tenant's authority.

Digital Asset Links for the verified Android App Link ``/app/sso-return`` (from
``KERP_ANDROID_APP_PACKAGE`` + ``KERP_ANDROID_APP_CERT_FINGERPRINTS``).

post.description:
Register this field device for the signed-in user and bind the session to it.

A new device gets its wipe secret in this response, once (store it per account). `pin`
sets the device's field PIN, once: a sign-in on the device later keeps it.

409.description: Another account's device, or session; `code: PIN_ALREADY_SET` when `pin` is sent for a device that has a PIN

Set a new field PIN for this device, from a signed-in session of the device (diff
§4.2: the PIN is changed after an online sign-in; the old PIN is not needed). Clears the

post.description:
The revoked device confirms it wiped its local store (records, outbox, media, keys),
with the wipe secret its enrolment returned.

Rate-limited per client address before anything else (T-0212, TD-298): every refusal is
audited, so an unlimited caller could grow the ledger at will. The lock-out never looks
at the device, so its ``429`` reveals nothing about it.

AccessRequestApprove.title: AccessRequestApprove
AccessRequestApprove.description:
``POST /access-requests/{id}/approve``: the persona(s) and site scope to grant.

They are added to any direct grants the requester already holds on the project. PER-09
together with a hold-authority persona needs ``confirm_sod: true`` (else 409
``sod_confirmation_required``, TD-151).

AccessRequestCreate.title: AccessRequestCreate
AccessRequestCreate.description:
``POST /access-requests``: ask for access to a project.

``lookup_ticket``: the ticket of a code lookup (``GET /lobby/projects/by-code/{code}``) for
this project. A user's **first** request for a project needs it when the user is external,
or internal and the project is not listed in the lobby; a new request after an earlier
rejected or withdrawn one needs none.

sod_warning.title: Sod Warning
sod_warning.description: PER-09 together with a hold-authority persona (confirmed with confirm_sod)

AccessRequestError.title: AccessRequestError
AccessRequestError.description:
A refusal with a machine-readable ``code`` (e.g. ``ACCESS_REQUEST_COOLDOWN``).
``retry_after``: when a new request becomes allowed (cooldown only).

AccessRequestRead.title: AccessRequestRead
AccessRequestRead.description:
One of the caller's own requests (the lobby's "Active requests" panel).

``rejection_reason``: the decider's reason, on a ``rejected`` request only.
``request_again_at``: on a ``rejected`` request, when "Request again" is allowed (the
re-request cooldown); ``null`` when a new request is allowed now, and on every other status.

AccessRequestReject.title: AccessRequestReject
AccessRequestReject.description: ``POST /access-requests/{id}/reject``: an optional reason, shown to the requester.

AdminGrantIn.title: AdminGrantIn
AdminGrantIn.description: ``POST /admin/grants``: give ``grant`` to the user (``system_admin`` callers only).

AdminGrantKind.title: AdminGrantKind
AdminGrantKind.description: The two tenant-level grants (``access.ADMIN_GRANTS``); neither is a persona.

sso.description: Present when the deployment offers Entra ID SSO

AuthConfigResponse.description: What the sign-in screen offers. No secret, no tenant id.

CheckFinding.title: CheckFinding
CheckFinding.description: A rule of the set that did not pass. ``message`` is the user-readable reason.

offline_window_days.description: Days an offline device may work, 1-14

offline_grace_hours.description: Hours after the server session ended that an offline device may keep unlocking with the PIN and queueing changes (1 to 24 x offline_window_days)

max_checkout_clock_skew_s.description: Largest device clock skew in seconds allowed when taking work offline

DeploymentSettingsRead.description: The effective deployment settings (the shipped defaults until a System admin edits).

device_id.description: Generated by the client once per installation

DriftEntryRead.description: A project rule that differs from the tenant default (or a default the project lacks).

A project found in the lobby. ``member``: the caller already has effective access to

MagicLinkRedeemRequest.description: Spend a magic link: a new session (on an enrolled device: bound to it, PIN kept).

MyProject.title: MyProject
MyProject.description: One project of the caller, for the project picker (T-0042).

No pin over the API: a pin is cleared by the action of the module that set it, and an
API caller has no such action.

NotificationSent.title: NotificationSent
NotificationSent.description: The stored notification and each channel's outcome.

OverrideDecisionInput.description: Body of an approval or rejection.

PendingAccessRequest.description: A pending request, as the project's PER-09 holders (and System admins) see it.

refresh_token.description: The refresh token, for the native app only (its `Origin` is on `KERP_NATIVE_APP_ORIGINS`); ignored on every other request, which uses the cookie

failed_offline.title: Failed Offline
failed_offline.description: Wrong PINs entered on the device while offline since its last successful unlock, not yet reported: counted before this attempt with the same escalation. Applied only when the attempt runs (not on 429): keep the count until another answer

PinUnlockRequest.title: PinUnlockRequest
PinUnlockRequest.description:
The PIN. The device's refresh token comes from the refresh cookie (the native app:
``refresh_token`` here): both are required, a PIN alone is never a credential.

PolygonGeoJSON.title: PolygonGeoJSON
PolygonGeoJSON.description: A GeoJSON ``Polygon`` in WGS84: ``[lon, lat]`` positions, exterior ring first.

PresignedRead.title: PresignedRead
PresignedRead.description: A request the client sends straight to object storage before ``expires_at``.

ProjectCreate.title: ProjectCreate
ProjectCreate.description:
``POST /projects``. The tenant comes from the token, never from the body.

``status``, ``site_timezone``, ``currency_code`` and ``locale`` may be omitted: the service
then takes the deployment's defaults for new projects (settings module, T-0044). They
cannot be ``null``.

ProjectUpdate.title: ProjectUpdate
ProjectUpdate.description: ``PATCH /projects/{id}``: only the given fields change; ``spatial_bounds: null`` clears.

refresh_token.title: Refresh Token
refresh_token.description: The refresh token, for the native app only (its `Origin` is on `KERP_NATIVE_APP_ORIGINS`); ignored on every other request, which uses the cookie

RefreshRequest.title: RefreshRequest
RefreshRequest.description: Optional body of ``/auth/refresh``: only the native app sends its refresh token here.

ResolvedColumn.title: ResolvedColumn
ResolvedColumn.description: A saved column as the register shows it; ``missing``: no longer in the catalogue.

RuleInput.title: RuleInput
RuleInput.description:
Body of ``PUT .../rules/{rule_key}``: add a rule, or edit the rule with that key.

The origin of a rule is set by copies only; ``locked`` is honoured on the tenant layer
(locking a default) and refused on the project layer.

RuleSetUpdatesRead.title: RuleSetUpdatesRead
RuleSetUpdatesRead.description: ``GET .../rule-sets/{set}/updates``: the per-rule diff against the parent default.

RuleUpdateRead.title: RuleUpdateRead
RuleUpdateRead.description: One rule of an upgrade offer: the set's rule (``current``) next to the new default.

SavedViewCreate.title: SavedViewCreate
SavedViewCreate.description:
``POST .../views`` (also "save as"). The owner is the caller; the project is the path's.

``team_id`` names the team of a ``team`` view and is given for no other visibility.
``is_default`` is allowed on ``private`` (the caller's default) and ``project`` (the
project default, Project Administrator only) views.

SavedViewRead.title: SavedViewRead
SavedViewRead.description:
A view as loaded: its configuration plus which referenced columns are missing.

``missing_columns`` lists every id (from columns, filter, sort, group-by) the register's
catalogue no longer has; the register skips them. It is empty when the register has
no catalogue registered (nothing can be checked).

SavedViewUpdate.title: SavedViewUpdate
SavedViewUpdate.description:
``PATCH .../views/{id}``: edit, rename, share, make default; only given fields change.

``filter``, ``group_by`` and ``team_id`` may be ``null`` (clears them). The register
of a view never changes.

verifier.description: The app-generated verifier whose S256 hash `/start` received

SsoExchangeRequest.description: The native app redeems the single-use exchange code of its App Link (diff §4.5).

start_url.title: Start Url
start_url.description: Open by top-level navigation (web) or in the system browser (Android, with `device_id` and `app_challenge`)

SsoOption.title: SsoOption
SsoOption.description:
Entra ID SSO is offered: the promoted, default sign-in for company staff (diff §4.5
*SSO promoted, password kept*). Password sign-in stays available for everyone.

refresh_expires_in.title: Refresh Expires In
refresh_expires_in.description: Seconds until the login session ends (sign-in + 12 h); then sign in again

session_expires_at.title: Session Expires At
session_expires_at.description: When the login session ends (sign-in + 12 h, the refresh token's end): the same on every rotation and PIN unlock. A field client starts its offline grace here

refresh_token.title: Refresh Token
refresh_token.description: Native app only (`Origin` on `KERP_NATIVE_APP_ORIGINS`): the refresh token, kept in the device keystore. Absent for every other caller (cookie transport)

TokenResponse.title: TokenResponse
TokenResponse.description:
The access token. The refresh token is the ``httpOnly`` refresh cookie (diff §4.2,
TD-203); only a request from an allow-listed native-app ``Origin`` gets it in the body
(``refresh_token``, T-0043) instead.

TryResult.title: TryResult
TryResult.description:
What a rule does with a sample context (ADR 0004 §6). Never persisted.

CEL rules: ``pass`` when the expression returns ``true``, ``fail`` on any other value,
``error`` when it cannot be evaluated; ``value`` is the result (KERP CEL JSON). A ``check``
rule that does not pass also returns the ``finding`` ``run_checks`` would log. Regex rules
(sample ``{"text": ...}``): ``pass`` when the pattern matches (``autolink``: every match;
``p6_grammar``: a full match), with the matches and their named groups.

TryRuleInput.title: TryRuleInput
TryRuleInput.description:
Body of ``POST .../rules/{rule_key}/try``: a sample context and, optionally, a draft
rule to try instead of the stored one (nothing is saved either way).

UnlockRequestCreate.title: UnlockRequestCreate
UnlockRequestCreate.description: Body of an unlock request: the ADR that justifies unlocking (ADR 0004 §5).

UploadCreate.title: UploadCreate
UploadCreate.description:
``POST /uploads/projects/{project_id}/files``: what the client is about to upload.

``sha256`` is the client's hex digest of the bytes; the server recomputes it before the
file becomes available. ``size_bytes`` is signed into the upload URL.

UploadTicket.title: UploadTicket
UploadTicket.description: The new file record and the presigned ``PUT`` for its bytes.

UserCreate.title: UserCreate
UserCreate.description: ``POST /admin/users``: an account without credentials (invite / reset set them).

UserLookupRequest.title: UserLookupRequest
UserLookupRequest.description: ``POST /admin/users/lookup``: an exact e-mail, in the body so it stays out of URLs.

is_internal.title: Is Internal
is_internal.description: Internal staff: read-only, derived at sign-in and account creation

wipe_secret.title: Wipe Secret
wipe_secret.description: The secret enrolment returned. Required: without it, or with a wrong one, the answer is the uniform refusal
